evidence.quote: To support explicit CoT post-training, we construct reference reasoning traces for each task.
Engine, we construct traces using predefined templates populated with their original annotated step labels
and short answers. For HAR, Sleep, and TSR, we generate reference traces using Qwen3.5-27B, following
distillation pipeline. We prompt Qwen3.5-27B to answer each question while conditioning it on rendered
traces that interleave natural language reasoning with explicit segment-selection calls, then post-process them
from a teacher model. In all cases the trace is used only to shape training and is never emitted at inference.
we generate one with a distillation pipeline following Messica et al. (2026), as for HAR and Sleep.

notes: TSR consequence/judgment QA supports decision_support, while ECG and Engine support diagnosis and HAR/Sleep support classification. No numerical forecasting or synthesis is demonstrated. Accuracy/F1 and latency are reported, but there is no runtime execution-validity evaluation, chronological split or availability audit, or realized downstream utility. The no-test-set checkpoint-selection statement at lines 1650-1652 is general evaluation hygiene, not temporal validity. Standard decoding/logit-lens analyses, unchanged backbone components, baselines, and future adaptive-computation RL are not separate contributed modules. Reconciliation retains the existing distillation ID and adds the independently reusable reference reasoning training traces; no existing module is dropped or split.
